questions.q: A desert insect kept in a dry container in Sokoto excretes mainly uric acid rather than ammonia. What is the main advantage of this to the insect?
options: It is more soluble in water and is easily washed away.
It conserves water because uric acid is excreted as a semi-solid paste.
It diffuses rapidly through the body surface as a gas.
It can be reused directly as a source of energy without breakdown.
questions.explanation: In a dry habitat the main excretory problem is conserving water. Uric acid is relatively insoluble and is eliminated as a semi-solid paste, so much less water is lost than would be needed to excrete ammonia.

questions.q: Many plants store waste substances such as tannins, resins and calcium oxalate crystals in their leaves. How are these wastes mainly removed from the plant?
options: By active transport through the root hairs into the soil
By diffusion through open stomata as gases
By being broken down completely into oxygen in the chloroplasts
questions.explanation: Plants cannot easily eliminate insoluble wastes such as tannins, resins and calcium oxalate crystals from living tissues. These wastes are mainly lost when old leaves senesce and fall off; stomata remove gases and water vapour, not such stored materials.

questions.q: A farmer in Minna notices that groundnut plants grow well on a nitrogen-poor soil. Which microorganism is mainly responsible for converting atmospheric nitrogen into usable compounds inside the root nodules of the groundnut?
questions.explanation: Rhizobium bacteria live symbiotically in the root nodules of legumes such as groundnut and fix atmospheric nitrogen into usable nitrogen compounds. Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter act later in the soil during nitrification.

questions.q: Early in the morning before sunrise, a fish pond near Warri is most likely to have its lowest dissolved oxygen level. This is mainly because during the night
options: photosynthesis stops while respiration by plants and animals continues to use oxygen
water temperature falls so oxygen is converted into hydrogen
decomposers stop breaking down dead matter in the pond
respiration stops while photosynthesis continues to release oxygen
questions.explanation: During darkness, photosynthesis stops, so no new oxygen is produced, while plants and animals continue respiring and using oxygen. Decomposition also continues, so dissolved oxygen reaches its lowest level near dawn.

questions.q: A fish farmer in Epe stocks a pond with tilapia. The population rises rapidly at first but later remains around 2,000 fish because food and space are limited. The value 2,000 represents the
options: birth rate of the tilapia population
carrying capacity of the pond for tilapia
questions.explanation: Carrying capacity is the maximum population size that the resources of a habitat can support over a period. The population levels off around 2,000 because food and space cannot support more tilapia.

questions.q: A student in Ibadan places the stem of a white rose in water containing red dye. After some hours, red streaks appear in the petals. Which tissue mainly transported the dye?
questions.explanation: The red dye moves upward with the water stream, which is transported through xylem vessels. Phloem mainly transports organic food materials such as sugars.

questions.q: In the classification of living things, which taxonomic group comes immediately below class?
questions.explanation: The standard taxonomic hierarchy is kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus and species. Therefore the group immediately below class is order.

questions.q: A plant collected from a shady part of a school compound in Ilesa has true roots, stems and leaves, but produces spores in sporangia on the underside of its fronds. It is best classified as a
questions.explanation: Ferns are vascular plants with true roots, stems and leaves, and they reproduce by spores produced in sporangia, often on the underside of fronds. Mosses lack true vascular roots and stems in the same sense, while gymnosperms and angiosperms reproduce by seeds.

questions.q: A community near a fast-flowing river in Benue records many cases of onchocerciasis. Which measure most directly targets the vector of this disease?
options: Treating all patients with antimalarial drugs
Draining all stagnant pools of water around the village
Applying larvicides to the river to control blackfly larvae
Using insecticide-treated bed nets at night
questions.explanation: Onchocerciasis is transmitted by blackflies, which breed in fast-flowing rivers. Applying larvicides to the river interrupts the vector's breeding cycle. Draining stagnant water targets mosquitoes, and bed nets at night do not effectively protect against day-biting blackflies.

questions.q: A health worker in Kano advises people to wash their hands after using the toilet to prevent typhoid fever. This advice works mainly because the typhoid organism is transmitted through
questions.explanation: Typhoid fever spreads mainly by the faecal-oral route, through food or water contaminated with faeces. Washing hands after using the toilet reduces the chance of transferring the organism to food or drinking water.

questions.q: A student in Enugu accidentally touches a hot pot and withdraws his hand before he feels the pain. Which part of the nervous system coordinates this rapid withdrawal?
questions.explanation: The withdrawal is a reflex action coordinated by the spinal cord through a reflex arc, allowing a quick response before the pain sensation reaches the brain. The cerebrum is involved in conscious sensation, the cerebellum in balance, and the medulla in vital involuntary functions.

questions.q: A herder in Maiduguri treks for hours under a hot sun and his body needs to conserve water. Which hormone increases water reabsorption by making the kidney collecting ducts more permeable to water?
questions.explanation: Dehydration stimulates the release of ADH, which increases the permeability of the collecting ducts to water and reduces water loss in urine. Aldosterone mainly regulates sodium and potassium balance, while adrenaline and glucagon affect responses to stress and blood glucose respectively.

questions.q: A pollen grain from a hibiscus flower in Enugu lands on the stigma. Which structure grows down the style to deliver the male gametes to the ovule?
questions.explanation: After pollination, the pollen grain germinates and forms a pollen tube that grows through the style towards the ovule. The pollen tube carries the male gametes for fertilisation. The filament supports the anther, the placenta is not a structure in this flower's pollen pathway, and the radicle is the embryonic root.

questions.q: A student in Oyo is studying the first stage of glucose breakdown in a cell. In which part of the cell does glycolysis take place?
questions.explanation: Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm, where glucose is broken down to pyruvate with a small yield of ATP and NADH. The mitochondrial matrix and inner membrane are sites of later stages of aerobic respiration, not glycolysis.

questions.q: A student in Enugu examines a mitochondrion from a rat liver cell. The enzymes of the Krebs cycle are mainly located in the
questions.explanation: The enzymes of the Krebs cycle are found in the mitochondrial matrix, where acetyl-CoA is oxidised and carbon dioxide is released. The inner mitochondrial membrane mainly contains the electron transport chain and ATP synthase.

questions.q: In pea plants, the gene pairs A/a and B/b are on different chromosomes. A plant of genotype AaBb is crossed with a plant of genotype aabb. What fraction of the offspring is expected to have genotype aabb?
questions.explanation: Because the genes are on different chromosomes, the AaBb parent forms AB, Ab, aB and ab gametes in equal proportions. The aabb parent forms only ab gametes, so the chance of an aabb offspring is the chance of an ab gamete from the first parent, which is 1/4.

questions.q: A student in Enugu observes a cell that has no membrane-bound nucleus and no mitochondria. Which type of cell is it most likely to be?
questions.explanation: Bacterial cells are prokaryotic and lack a membrane-bound nucleus and mitochondria. Yeast cells, palisade mesophyll cells and white blood cells are eukaryotic and contain a nucleus and mitochondria.

questions.q: A ligament is best described as a structure that
options: secretes synovial fluid into the joint cavity
joins one bone to another bone at a joint
forms the hard matrix of bone
joins a muscle to a bone
questions.explanation: Ligaments are tough fibrous connective tissues that connect one bone to another across a joint and help stabilize it. A tendon attaches skeletal muscle to bone, while synovial fluid is secreted by the synovial membrane and bone matrix is formed mainly by osteoblasts and mineral salts.

questions.q: In the upper arm, the biceps and triceps are described as antagonistic muscles because
options: when one contracts, the other relaxes to produce opposite movements
they contract only when the arm is completely at rest
they are attached to the same bone and perform identical actions
they both contract together to produce the same movement
questions.explanation: Antagonistic muscles act as a pair at a joint because contraction of one produces a movement opposite to that produced by the other. In the arm, the biceps flexes the elbow while the triceps extends it, so they do not perform identical actions.

questions.q: A potato strip from Jos is placed in 0.3 mol/dm³ sucrose solution and its length decreases slightly. Which process best explains the decrease?
options: Sucrose enters the potato cells by diffusion and makes them shrink.
Water leaves the potato cells by osmosis into the more concentrated sucrose solution.
Salts leave the potato cells by active transport, causing the cells to lose water.
Water enters the potato cells by osmosis from the sucrose solution.
questions.explanation: In the sucrose solution, the external solution has a lower water potential than the potato cell sap, so water moves out of the cells by osmosis and the tissue loses turgor. Sucrose does not enter by simple diffusion to cause shrinkage, and water would enter only if the external solution were more dilute than the cell sap.

questions.q: After a person in Kaduna drinks a large volume of water, the kidneys produce a large volume of dilute urine. This is due to
questions.explanation: Antidiuretic hormone increases water reabsorption from the collecting ducts of the kidney. After drinking a large volume of water, ADH secretion decreases, so more water remains in the urine and a large volume of dilute urine is produced.

questions.q: A farmer in Oyo State notices that weeds reduce maize yield mainly because the weeds
options: provide shade that increases the rate of photosynthesis in maize
fix atmospheric nitrogen for the maize plants
compete with the maize for light, water and mineral salts
decompose maize roots and release growth hormones
questions.explanation: Weeds reduce maize yield mainly by competing with the crop for the same resources, especially light, water and mineral salts. They do not generally increase maize photosynthesis or supply fixed nitrogen, and decomposition is carried out mainly by microorganisms.

questions.q: Tomato seedlings grown in waterlogged soil in Ibadan show poor uptake of mineral salts even though the salts are present in the soil. Which factor most directly explains this?
options: The root hair surface becomes too wet for diffusion of salts
Transpiration pull stops completely when the soil is waterlogged
Oxygen shortage in the soil reduces respiration and active transport in root hair cells
Water in the soil dilutes the mineral salts below the concentration needed for osmosis
questions.explanation: Mineral salts are absorbed mainly by active transport, which requires energy from respiration. Waterlogging reduces oxygen supply to root cells, lowering respiration and ATP production, so active uptake of salts is impaired.

questions.q: A student in Ilorin has blood group AB. Which statement about the ABO antigens and antibodies in his blood is correct?
options: His red cells have both A and B antigens, and his plasma has neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies
His red cells have A antigen but no B antigen, and his plasma has anti-B antibodies
His red cells have neither A nor B antigens, and his plasma has both anti-A and anti-B antibodies
His red cells have B antigen but no A antigen, and his plasma has anti-A antibodies
questions.explanation: AB individuals have both A and B antigens on their red blood cells and no naturally occurring anti-A or anti-B antibodies in plasma. The absence of these antibodies prevents their plasma from agglutinating their own red cells.

questions.q: Which feature of mature xylem vessels in a flowering plant best enables them to transport water rapidly from the roots to the leaves?
options: They are living cells with dense cytoplasm and many mitochondria
They are dead and hollow, with lignified walls and no end walls between vessel elements
They have sieve plates at their end walls to allow cytoplasmic streaming
They are narrow cells lined with root hairs that actively pump water
questions.explanation: Mature xylem vessels form continuous dead, hollow tubes with lignified walls, offering little resistance to the upward flow of water. Living cytoplasm or sieve plates would obstruct the rapid movement of water.

questions.q: A community health officer in Kano advises families to cover their mouths when coughing and to keep rooms well ventilated because a patient has pulmonary tuberculosis. This advice mainly limits the spread of the pathogen through
options: droplets in the air from coughing or sneezing
direct contact with the patient's unbroken skin
questions.explanation: Pulmonary tuberculosis is caused by bacteria spread in airborne droplets released when an infected person coughs or sneezes. Ventilation dilutes these droplets and reduces the chance of others inhaling them.

questions.q: A boy in Ilorin has ringworm on his scalp. Which practice most directly reduces spread of the infection to other children in his class?
options: Avoid sharing combs, caps and towels and treat the affected skin
Avoid walking barefoot on damp soil
Boil all drinking water before use
questions.explanation: Ringworm is a fungal skin infection spread by contact with infected skin or contaminated personal items such as combs, caps and towels. Treating the affected skin and avoiding sharing such items reduces transmission; water, mosquitoes and damp soil are not the main routes.

questions.q: A trader in Onitsha is suddenly frightened by a loud noise. Her heart beats faster and her pupils widen. Which hormone is mainly responsible for these immediate responses?
questions.explanation: Adrenaline is secreted by the adrenal medulla during sudden stress and produces rapid fight-or-flight responses such as a faster heartbeat and dilated pupils. Thyroxine mainly raises the long-term basal metabolic rate, while insulin lowers blood glucose.

questions.q: A pregnant woman in Aba is told that the fluid surrounding and protecting the fetus is produced by a membrane. Which membrane is this?
questions.explanation: The amnion is the membrane that encloses the fetus in amniotic fluid, which cushions it against mechanical shock and helps prevent drying. The chorion contributes to placenta formation, while the allantois helps form umbilical blood vessels.

questions.q: A grasshopper collected from a farm in Keffi obtains oxygen from the air through a system of tubes. Oxygen reaches its body cells mainly through the
questions.explanation: Air enters a grasshopper through spiracles and passes along tracheae, but the finest branches, the tracheoles, deliver oxygen directly to the body cells. Spiracles are only the openings of the respiratory system.

questions.q: During quiet expiration in a healthy person in Jos, which change occurs in the thorax?
options: The diaphragm relaxes and moves upwards while the ribs move downwards and inwards.
The external intercostal muscles contract and increase the volume of the thorax.
The diaphragm contracts and flattens while the ribs move upwards and outwards.
The lungs actively contract and pull the ribs inwards.
questions.explanation: During quiet expiration, the diaphragm relaxes and returns to its dome shape, while the ribs move downwards and inwards. These changes reduce thoracic volume, increase pressure in the lungs, and force air out. Contraction of the diaphragm and external intercostals occurs during inspiration.

questions.q: A woman in Owerri is a carrier of haemophilia (X^H X^h), and her husband is not haemophiliac (X^H Y). What is the probability that a son born to them will have haemophilia?
questions.explanation: The sons receive a Y chromosome from their father and either X^H or X^h from their mother with equal probability. A son with X^hY has haemophilia, so the probability among sons is 1/2. The probability that a child of either sex is affected is 1/4, which is not what the question asks.

questions.q: A liver cell from a goat in Makurdi is exposed to a fat-soluble drug. The cell responds by increasing the surface area of an organelle that detoxifies the drug and synthesises lipids. Which organelle is most directly involved?
questions.explanation: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum is abundant in liver cells, where its enzymes help detoxify drugs and synthesise lipids. Rough endoplasmic reticulum is mainly associated with protein synthesis, while the Golgi apparatus modifies and packages proteins and lysosomes contain digestive enzymes.

questions.q: A student in Ibadan studies a pancreas cell that secretes digestive enzymes. In which sequence are the enzymes moved from where they are made to the outside of the cell?
options: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum → lysosome → Golgi apparatus → cell membrane
Rough endoplasmic reticulum → ribosome → Golgi apparatus → secretory vesicle
Nucleus → mitochondrion → Golgi apparatus → secretory vesicle
Ribosome → rough endoplasmic reticulum → Golgi apparatus → secretory vesicle
questions.explanation: Secretory enzymes are proteins made on ribosomes attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum, then modified and packaged by the Golgi apparatus into vesicles that fuse with the cell membrane. The other sequences place synthesis or processing in the wrong organelle.

questions.q: A new allele that makes maize plants in Zaria tolerate drought appears in a population. Which process is the original source of this new allele?
questions.explanation: Mutation changes the DNA base sequence and is the original source of new alleles. Crossing over, independent assortment and random fertilisation only reshuffle existing alleles into new combinations.

questions.q: A population of frogs in Cross River State is divided when a new wide river changes course. After many generations, the frogs on either side have different mating calls and no longer interbreed. Which process has occurred?
questions.explanation: Geographic separation prevented gene flow between the two frog populations, and accumulated genetic differences eventually produced reproductive isolation and a new species. This process is speciation, specifically allopatric speciation.

questions.q: A tailor in Aba rotates her arm freely at the shoulder during work. Which type of joint makes this movement possible?
questions.explanation: A ball-and-socket joint has a rounded bone end fitting into a socket, allowing movement in several planes, including rotation at the shoulder. Hinge, pivot and gliding joints permit more restricted types of movement.

questions.q: A student in Enugu studies the movement of substances across a selectively permeable membrane. Which statement describes active transport?
options: It uses energy to move a substance against its concentration gradient.
It depends only on the random motion of particles down a concentration gradient.
It moves substances from a higher to a lower concentration without carrier proteins or energy.
It moves water from a region of lower solute concentration to a region of higher solute concentration.
questions.explanation: Active transport uses energy, usually from ATP, and carrier proteins to move substances against a concentration gradient. Osmosis and diffusion are passive, while movement from a higher to a lower concentration without carrier proteins or energy describes diffusion.

questions.q: During a hot afternoon in Sokoto, a laboratory animal is given a drug that increases the permeability of the collecting duct of the kidney to water. Compared with before the drug, the urine produced will most likely be
options: larger in volume and more dilute
larger in volume and richer in proteins
smaller in volume and more concentrated
unchanged in volume but richer in glucose
questions.explanation: Increasing the permeability of the collecting duct to water allows more water to be reabsorbed into the blood. Therefore, less water remains in the urine, making it smaller in volume and more concentrated. The opposite effect would make urine larger in volume and dilute.

questions.q: Which waste product of metabolism is removed from the body mainly through the lungs?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide produced during respiration diffuses from the blood into the alveoli and is breathed out. Urea is mainly removed by the kidneys, while bile salts are excreted in bile.
